episode.tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
episode.title: What Really Happens When You Ask AI a Question?
episode.disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario based on researched conditions in Cameroon's South-West cocoa region

onScreen.text: Brown cocoa pods near Kumba. The chatbot: “Spray product X at dose Y.”
onScreen.emphasis: No question about her farm. No source.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Ebot grows cocoa near Kumba, in Cameroon's South-West. After heavy rains, her pods turn brown.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: A chatbot on her phone answers: spray product X at dose Y. Nobody asked where her farm is.

onScreen.title: What Really Happens When You Ask AI a Question?
onScreen.subtitle: Tokens · prediction · context · tools. Built with a cocoa cooperative near Kumba.

onScreen.title: What the crew heard
onScreen.app: Meme Cocoa Farmers Cooperative Society · Messages

messages.text: Ebot: Brown pods since the rains. Njume comes next week. What do I spray?
Ebot: Ask about my farm before you answer. And say where the advice comes from.
Njume: I cover all the member farms alone. Many farmers here never see an extension officer.
Njume: I keep the cooperative's advice sheet. Questions come faster than I can visit.
Njume: Products and doses come to me, not from a machine.

steps.title: The gap
steps.detail: Ebot and Njume set the spec

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Tanyi, Ebot's message: brown pods since the rains, the field agent comes next week, what do I spray?

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Njume, the only field agent, keeps a checked guidance sheet. His rule: products and doses come to him, not from a machine.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: No context about her farm, no source. Ebot and Njume told us what they need. We build to that.

scenes.label: Decide: what AI should and should not do

left.title: General chatbot
items: No source, names a product anyway

right.title: Cooperative assistant
items: Reads only Njume's sheet, shows source
Product and dose: to Njume, never the model

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: A general chatbot knows nothing about Ebot's farm. It predicts a fluent answer, no source.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Ebot's rule: ask about her farm first. Njume's rule: answer only from his sheet, and show the source.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Njume's hard rule becomes ours. No product name, no dose, ever comes from the model. Those go to him.

scenes.label: Decide: what happens when you ask

onScreen.title: From your question to its answer

nodes.label: Context
nodes.sub: All it can see right now

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: First, tokens. Your question is cut into pieces: words, parts of words, sometimes single characters.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Then it predicts: it was trained to guess the next word from the words before it.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Its context is its working memory. Anything not in there, it does not know.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Alone, it cannot check anything. With a tool, it asks, your software fetches a checked page into its context.

onScreen.app: Meme Cocoa Farmers Cooperative Society · Assistant

items.text: What she sees: brown patches on pods
3 · Prune on time, before the rains
4 · Black pod after heavy rain: take off diseased pods, keep the farm clear, spray on the cooperative's schedule

ui.title: Context sent to the model
lines: Question: brown pods, what to spray?
Farm: near Kumba · ripening · heavy rain

messages.text: Brown pods since the rains. What do I spray?
Take off the diseased pods, keep the farm clear, spray on the cooperative's schedule.
Source: Guidance sheet, entry 4, updated by Njume.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: I ask before I answer: crop stage, where, when the rains came, what Ebot sees.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Njume's guidance sheet. Kito, why his sheet and not the whole internet?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: My answer is only as good as the page I read. Retrieval puts the matching entry, entry four, into my context.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Then I answer plainly and show the source: guidance sheet, entry four, updated by Njume.

scenes.label: Constraint and fix: the confident guess

steps.title: The confident guess
steps.detail: No source, no question about her farm

messages.text: Which product and what dose should I spray?
Spray product X at dose Y every week. Problem solved.
Which product and what dose should I spray?
Product and dose: not covered by the guidance sheet. Sent to Njume, who will reply.

ui.title: Why a wrong answer can sound so sure
lines: Rewarded in training: a confident guess
Fluent is not the same as right

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: Simple. Spray product X at dose Y every week, and your problem is solved.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: No product entry in my sheet, so I will not guess. Not covered, sent to Njume.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: That is a hallucination: a fluent answer that is wrong. OpenAI researchers showed that training and testing reward a confident guess over saying I don't know.

scenes.label: Constraint and fix: when the network is down

steps.title: A documented constraint
steps.detail: Networks fail. The tool must not.

ui.title: Connectivity
lines: Documented: months without internet in this region (2017)
Design rule: it must work when the network does not

steps.title: Queue and fallback
steps.detail: Nothing is lost; a person always answers

items.text: Ebot · brown pods · queued on the phone
Unanswered → Njume by text or visit

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: In twenty seventeen, the two English-speaking regions lost the internet for three months. Kito, this must work offline.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: I queue questions on the phone. Unanswered ones reach Njume by text or a visit.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Ebot asks again. I ask stage, place, what she sees, then answer from entry four with its source.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Product and dose? Not from the model. Send to Njume. A person answers that.

onScreen.title: Who owns this assistant?
items: The cooperative owns sheet and assistant
Njume writes the sheet; the AI only reads
Questions, locations, value stay with members
Accountable: the cooperative and its agent

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: The cooperative owns the sheet and the assistant. Njume maintains it; the assistant only reads. Questions, locations and any value stay with the members.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: If advice is wrong, the cooperative and its agent answer for it, not the AI. Tokens, prediction, context, tool. Right context, a checked source, a person to escalate to.

lines.text: Build challenge: take one question you ask AI at work. Write down the context it needs. Add: tell me where this comes from. Compare the answers.

tanyi.name: Tanyi
tanyi.role: AI engineer and instructor, the animated host. Middle-aged Black African man. Calm, direct, practical. Has built and operated real systems.

amara.name: Amara
amara.role: Curious learner who asks the questions beginners are thinking.

kito.name: Kito
kito.role: Small AI assistant who demonstrates concepts and occasionally makes believable mistakes.

hallucinator.name: The Hallucinator
hallucinator.role: Mischievous. Represents confident but incorrect AI output.

gatekeeper.name: The Gatekeeper
gatekeeper.role: Represents security, privacy, governance and human approval.
